learning_outcomes.text: Applies correctly the principles of basic knowledge of general chemistry, organic and inorganic chemistry in engineering.

Constructs the electronic configuration of any atom or ion in the Periodic Table. Interprets atomic and periodic properties. Predicts the products of typical inorganic precipitation, acid-base, or gas-forming reactions. Predicts the products of an inorganic redox reaction. Constructs the chemical bonds of molecules or ions. Explains the physical-chemical properties and interactions of matter based on atomic and chemical bond models. Relates the structure of organic compounds to different physical and chemical properties.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Matter: atoms, the nuclear atom. Inside the atom: Observation of the atom: characteristics of light, quanta and photons, atomic spectra and levels, wave properties of electrons. Atomic models: atomic orbitals, quantum numbers and atomic orbitals, electron spin, hydrogen electronic structure. Structures of multi-electron atoms: energy in orbitals, Aufbau principle, electronic configurations of atoms, electronic configurations of ions.

Electronic structure and the periodic table. Periodicity of atomic properties: atomic radius, ionic radius, ionization potentials, ionization potential and metallic character, inert pair effect, diagonal relationships, electron affinity. Chemistry and the periodic table: s-block elements, p-block elements, d-block elements.

Chemical bonds: ionic bonds: Lewis structures for atoms and ions, lattice enthalpies, properties of compounds. Covalent bonds: from atoms to molecules, the octet rule and Lewis structures. Structures of polyatomic species: Lewis structures, resonance, formal charge. Exceptions to the octet rule: radicals and diradicals, expanded valence levels. Ionic vs. covalent bonding. Molecular geometry. Intermolecular forces.

Quantity in chemistry, the mole, molar mass, measurement of compounds. Determination of chemical formulas: mass percentage composition, determination of empirical formulas, determination of molecular formulas. Solutions in chemistry: molarity, dilution.

Chemical equations and chemical reactions: how chemical reactions are symbolized, how chemical equations are balanced. Concept of acid and base. Reactions between acids and bases: acids and bases in aqueous solutions, strong and weak acids and bases, acid and basic character in the periodic table, neutralization, gas formation. Redox reactions: oxidation and reduction, oxidation numbers, oxidizing and reducing agents, balancing simple redox equations, classification of reactions.
How to use reaction stoichiometry: prediction in moles, prediction in masses, the volume of a solution needed for a reaction. Reaction limits: reaction yield, limiting reactants, combustion analysis.
Boyle's Law. Charles's Law. The ideal gas law. Mixtures of ideal gases.
Concept of equilibrium. Law of mass action. Equilibrium constant, degree of dissociation, heterogeneous equilibria. Factors affecting equilibrium. Acid-base equilibrium.
Galvanic cells; cell potential; cell notation; standard potentials; Nernst equation; electrolytic cells; Faraday's law; corrosion; practical batteries.
assessment_rules: Students must achieve a minimum grade of 3.5 in the second partial exam to average it with the first partial exam. The second sitting consists of a final exam that may include all topics. Fraudulent completion of any evaluative activity by any means results in the student being graded as failed for that activity.
